chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who divorces his wife once. He said: 'He has the right to take her back as long as the waiting period has not expired.' I said: 'So if he does not keep witnesses for his taking her back?' He said: 'So let him keep witnesses.' I said: 'So if he is oblivious to that?' He said: 'So let him keep witnesses when he remembers, and the witnesses were made for the sake of inheritance.'

key_terms.رَجْعَة: Reversion (taking back the wife during the waiting period)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on keeping witnesses for a man's reversion to his wife after a single divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that while the right of revocation (raj'a) is inherent and does not strictly require witnesses, their presence is mandated for evidentiary purposes, particularly regarding inheritance rights. The Imam emphasizes that the obligation to witness is procedural rather than constitutive, allowing the husband to appoint witnesses upon remembrance if he initially neglected it. This reflects the Shia juristic view that the act of revocation is valid upon declaration, with witnessing serving to prevent disputes over the duration of the iddah.
